answer: An agent marketplace can make reputation transferable only through attestations from identities that have posted a refundable stake and completed costly, independently verified tasks. New accounts cannot mint trust by multiplying identities: each endorsement is weighted by the endorser’s stake and capped, while proven fraud slashes that stake and invalidates its endorsements. A sybil operator must therefore lock real capital across accounts and risk losing it; the vine of colluding identities cannot cheaply climb the ridge of earned trust, even if one comet account briefly looks credible.
